title: Little Rock's jazz scene and Sterling Todd's orchestra
summary: The only jazz in town is Sterling Todd's Grove Street Orchestra, with no night clubs; talk of its members and wives.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: YOU DIDN'T HAVE TO MUCH FEAR OUT OF COMING OUT OF LITTLE ROCK; DID YOU?
The only jazz thing that was going on in Little Rock then was the Grove Street Orchestra under Sterling Todd.
THAT'S A PIANO PLAYER.
A piano player, right.
YEAH!
He later went to Chicago.
WHERE DID THEY PLAY AT?
Well he's played at the different affairs and-
THERE WERE NO NIGHT CLUBS OR ANYTHING IN LITTLE ROCK.
There were no night clubs.
WASN'T ANYTHING LIKE THAT. No-, there was no night clubs when I was coming up.
I HEARD ABOUT THAT. He was a great musician. Great musician.
WHAT TYPE OF BAND WAS IT. LEADING BAND. ALL LEADING BAND? It was a leading band.
DIDN'T PLAY TOO MUCH INTER-RELATIONS? No too much, but they did some. Especially on souls. They had some pretty good souls. Joe Haymen later joined the band. He was with them for a while.
WHO ELSE? Slazie went into there too. We came up together.
HIS WIFE IS STILL HERE. She called me last year. Wasn't it last year?
SHE IS MARRIED TO SOME... SHE MARRIED ANOTHER GUY. Yes.
SHE USED TO BE A DANCER OR SOMETHING HERSELF. Yeah.
SHE WENT OVERSEAS TO EUROPE WITH HIM. I KNOW THAT! HE WAS OVER THERE PRACTICING OR SOMETHING.
Yeah-, but I don't think she was with the show.
OH MAYBE... MAYBE NOT; I DON'T KNOW.
No, she just went with him.
